record.paper_title: Projection Algorithms: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Suppose each Ci is a subspace of a real Hilbert space, C = C1 ∩ ··· ∩ CN is nonempty, and z_{n+1} = P_{r(n+1)} z_n is the sequence generated by a random map r that hits every index in {1, ..., N} infinitely often. Fact 5.1 shows that this random-projection sequence converges weakly to a point of C. Must such convergence in the subspace case always improve to norm convergence, or can random projections onto subspaces converge only weakly?

evidence.quote: Fact 5.1 (Amemiya and Ando). [1] Suppose each Ci is a subspace. Then the sequence of random projections converges weakly to a point in C.
Open Problem 4. In Fact 5.1, can the convergence be only weak?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be a real Hilbert space and let $C_1, \dots, C_N$ be closed linear subspaces of $H$ with $C := C_1 \cap \cdots \cap C_N \neq \emptyset$. For each $i \in \{1,\dots,N\}$, let $P_i$ denote the orthogonal projection of $H$ onto $C_i$. Let $r : \mathbb{N} \to \{1,\dots,N\}$ be a control sequence that takes every value in $\{1,\dots,N\}$ infinitely often, and for an arbitrary starting point $z_0 \in H$ define
$$z_{n+1} = P_{r(n+1)} z_n.$$
It is known that $(z_n)$ converges weakly to some point of $C$. Determine whether the convergence must always be in norm. Equivalently: do there exist a Hilbert space $H$, finitely many closed subspaces $C_1,\dots,C_N$, a control $r$ hitting each index infinitely often, and an initial point $z_0$ such that the resulting sequence $(z_n)$ converges weakly but not in norm?
artifact.status_search_result: The Amemiya–Ando conjecture (that the weak convergence must be in norm) was disproved. A. Paszkiewicz (2012) constructed five closed subspaces of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space and a sequence of projections onto them for which the iterates fail to converge in norm. Kopecká and Müller (2014) refined this to three subspaces. Hence weak-but-not-norm convergence is possible.

status_evidence.title: Strange products of projections
status_evidence.snippet: Kopecká and Müller construct three orthogonal projections onto closed subspaces of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space whose random products do not converge in norm.
status_evidence.claim: A counterexample exists with only three subspaces, so weak convergence in the Amemiya–Ando theorem cannot in general be upgraded to norm convergence.

status_evidence.title: The Method of Alternating Projections (Ginat)
status_evidence.snippet: Paszkiewicz (2012) constructed five subspaces of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space and a sequence of projections that does not converge in norm, answering the Amemiya–Ando question negatively.
status_evidence.claim: Paszkiewicz produced a counterexample showing random projections onto subspaces can converge only weakly.
